items.title: 14.13 Analyse data and interpret air quality

blocks.text: The collected data are analysed to confirm or refute the hypothesis, and the results are interpreted and conclusions drawn. Analysing and interpreting air-quality data involves understanding the concentrations of the pollutants, identifying trends over time, and assessing the implications for public health and environmental policy. By carefully designing experiments and collecting and analysing data, a hypothesis about air quality can be tested and strategies for improving air quality can be made.

blocks.prompt: A city's PM2.5 readings are 180 at 8 am and 60 at 2 pm on the same day. Interpret these figures.
blocks.explanation: Both are in the AQI's unhealthy range or worse in the morning: 180 is unhealthy for everyone, 60 is moderate. The sharp fall after the morning peak points to rush-hour traffic and a night-time inversion that trapped particles until the sun warmed and mixed the air; the policy implication is to cut morning traffic emissions and warn sensitive groups to avoid early outdoor activity.

items: Analyse concentrations and trends over time, interpret for health and policy, conclude whether the hypothesis holds, and use the result to plan improvements.
